title: External assessment evidence packaging and RBAC gap plan
content:
Purpose:
This document captures coordination notes for an upcoming external security assessment (third-party attack surface review + targeted pen-test), and defines the evidence packaging and automation requirements we will hand to assessors. It also highlights RBAC v2 gaps that should be remediated before the test or explicitly scoped out, and a prioritized remediation plan for findings expected from the assessment.

Context / background:
- Request from procurement to enable a vendor-start date week of 2025-11-17.
- Vendor scope: externally facing infra + controller plane API fuzzing + limited host-level privilege escalation on a sandboxed Dedicated cluster.
- Our ask: provide a reproducible evidence bundle and a way to stream audit logs to vendor SIEM in read-only mode.
- Core constraints: cannot share customer PII; must sanitize any user identifiers.

Primary contacts:
- Aisha Patel (security lead) — aisha@redwood.ai — overall coordinator
- Diego Martinez (platform eng) — Diego will own RBAC snapshot and IAM exports
- Hannah Lee (observability) — audit log schema lead and SIEM export owner
- Marcus Chen (SRE) — evidence packaging and host sandbox creation
- Rita Singh (privacy counsel) — final approval on data sanitization

High-level scope (what vendor will test):
1) Public API endpoints (hosted API tier) excluding customer-managed private deployments
2) Web console authentication flows and session handling (console within our hosted control plane)
3) Controller plane APIs for model metadata and rollout operations (read/write) — limited to test namespace
4) Sandbox Dedicated cluster (isolated VPC) for host-level checks — no access to production tenants

Out-of-scope (explicit):
- Customer production datasets, customer-managed VPCs, and private on-prem installs
- Full lateral movement into production clusters
- Live PII exfiltration tests (we will simulate synthetic PII for any necessary validation)

Evidence packaging requirements (what we will hand to vendor):
- RBAC snapshot (RBAC-V2) as-of timestamped export: list of roles, role bindings, effective permissions per service account. Format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). Fields must include: object_type, object_id, principal_type, principal_id (hashed), permissions, created_at, source_file.
- Audit log bundle (30 days around test start): logs exported in gzipped ndjson with normalized timestamp (ISO8601 UTC). Logs must map to standard schema (see "Audit schema mapping" below).
- SIEM ingest config: temporary read-only API key + exported mapping file (log field -> SIEM field) and a sample ingest pipeline config for vendor Splunk/Elastic/QRadar connectors.
- Evidence index: human-readable index.md listing included files, short provenance notes, and canonical commands used to generate each file (so vendor can reproduce).
- Host sandbox snapshot: AMI/instance image metadata, kernel version, installed packages, snapshot of /etc/passwd and /etc/sudoers (sanitized), and a list of running containers at snapshot time.
- Playbook for evidence verification: set of scripts (bash + python) that verify cryptographic checksums and show how to replay audit log playback (no real secrets).

Audit schema mapping (observability lead):
- source_service: string (e.g., "controller-api", "console", "runtime-gateway")
- event_type: string (e.g., "auth.login", "model.create", "kv.cache.hit")
- timestamp: iso8601 string (UTC)
- actor: hashed_principal_id (sha256) and principal_type (user/service) — actual email/usernames must be redacted or hashed with salt stored in a vault
- actor_ip: ipv4/ipv6 or "REDACTED" for customer-originated traffic
- request_id: unique id per request
- resource: resource_type/resource_id (e.g., "model:mv2-3" or "cluster:ded-42")
- action: CRUD-style action (create/read/update/delete) + verb
- outcome: success | failure | error-code
- meta: free-form map encoded as JSON string (for extra fields)

(We will provide an OpenSearch ingestion template and a Splunk sourcetype example in the repo.)

RBAC v2 snapshot and expected gaps:
- Current state: RBAC v2 rollout started 2025-09; most infra services (controller, console, gRPC runtime) have migrated to role-based checks but legacy service tokens and some admin bindings still exist.
- Known gaps to remediate pre-test (high priority):
  * Legacy admin: 6 legacy admin tokens exist (JIRA-SEC-2341) — rotate/delete before handing access or explicitly exclude from scope.
  * Cross-tenant read: a utility service account (svc-search) still has read:item across tenant DB in the sandbox control plane. Need to scope down to test-namespace.
  * Wildcard role bindings: audit found bindings with resource:"*" on older clusters — need to tighten to explicit clusters.
- Medium priority: update documentation to reflect effective-permission computation for service account impersonation flows (edge case causes some roles to appear more permissive than effective runtime policy).

Remediation plan (prioritized):
- Immediate (before vendor start):
  1) Rotate/delete legacy admin tokens and produce token rotation proof (who rotated, when). Owner: Diego. Due: 2025-11-10. JIRA-SEC-2486-1.
  2) Export RBAC snapshot and run automated policy analyzer (script: infra/tools/rbac-audit.sh) — produce html summary. Owner: Diego + Hannah. Due: 2025-11-12. JIRA-SEC-2486-2.
  3) Create sandboxed Dedicated cluster and populate with synthetic tenants and synthetic PII dataset. Owner: Marcus. Due: 2025-11-14. JIRA-OPS-1177.
- Short term (1-3 weeks):
  1) Narrow svc-search permissions to namespace-scoped read only. Owner: Platform eng. Due: 2025-11-28.
  2) Replace wildcard role bindings with explicit resource lists in cluster-template. Owner: Release eng. Due: 2025-11-21.
  3) Add automated gating in CI that fails deployment if any binding uses resource:"*". Owner: Release eng. Due: 2025-12-03.
- Medium term (1-3 months):
  1) Implement RBAC policy simulator (live preview of effective permissions) in console to help troubleshoot impersonation edge cases. Owner: Product + Eng. Target: 2026-02-01.
  2) Formalize audit log retention mapping and SIEM retention contract for vendor testing (policy doc). Owner: Observability. Target: 2026-01-15.

Evidence automation runbook (draft):
- Generate RBAC snapshot:
  1) Run infra/tools/rbac-export --format ndjson --salt-vault=secret/rbac-salt --out=rbac-snapshot-20251112.ndjson
  2) Verify checksum: sha256sum rbac-snapshot-20251112.ndjson > rbac-snapshot.sha256
  3) Push to s3://redwood-evidence/2025-11/ (write-only bucket)

- Package audit logs:
  1) Use obs/exporter -> obs/exporter --start 2025-10-15 --end 2025-11-15 --normalize --mask-customer --out audit-bundle-20251112.ndjson.gz
  2) Run obs/validator --schema audit-schema-v1.json audit-bundle-20251112.ndjson.gz

- Create SIEM shim for vendor (temporary):
  1) Create read-only API key in obs (scoped to bucket and index) expire in 14 days
  2) Provide mapping file siem-mapping-splunk.json and sample ingest.conf

Communications plan and approvals:
- Privacy signoff required on sanitized sampling and any synthetic PII. Owner: Rita Singh. Slack channel: #sec-pen-test.
- Legal approval for vendor contract clauses that allow limited log ingestion and non-production data handling. Owner: procurement/legal.
- Internal pre-brief: 2025-11-13 09:30 PT — run-through of scope, show sandbox, quick demo of audit replay.

Workshop checklist for pre-brief (quick):
- [ ] Confirm vendor list and final SOW (Procurement)
- [ ] Provide RBAC snapshot (Diego)
- [ ] Provide audit log sample and schema (Hannah)
- [ ] Create sandbox and invite vendor SOC (Marcus)
- [ ] Approve sanitization plan (Rita)

Potential vendor questions we should anticipate:
- Can you prove that the RBAC snapshot is complete (how computed)? -> answer: provide command, hash, and a small verification script.
- Will the logs include customer traffic? -> answer: no, customer traffic will be redacted; we will provide synthetic requests that exercise same code paths.
- What happens if they find a critical privilege escalation in the sandbox? -> answer: immediate containment plan; if exploitable at scale we'll treat as P1 and follow incident runbook.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: Do we allow vendor to run authenticated write tests against controller APIs in the sandbox, or only read/fuzz? (security/plat)
- Q2: Should we provide pre-generated user sessions to the vendor or require them to generate their own during testing? (operational cost vs reproducibility)
- Q3: Confirm whether vendor SIEM integration should be direct push (we give keys) or via our replay tool (we push logs). Recommended: replay only for tighter control.

Appendix: example RBAC export line (ndjson)
{"object_type":"role","object_id":"role:svc-search-reader","principal_type":"service_account","principal_id":"sha256:abcdef...","permissions":["read:items","list:indices"],"created_at":"2025-09-02T18:21:34Z","source_file":"cluster-template-v2.yaml"}

Appendix: sample audit line (ndjson)
{"source_service":"controller-api","event_type":"model.update","timestamp":"2025-11-12T17:02:11Z","actor":"sha256:1234abcd...","actor_ip":"REDACTED","request_id":"req_01G7ZQ4Y","resource":"model:mv2-3","action":"update","outcome":"success","meta":"{\"payload_size\":1234}"}

Notes (freeform):
- Keep evidence bundle lean: vendors prefer clear reproducibility over gigantic raw logs.
- We should prepare to rotate the read-only keys immediately after the engagement ends.
- If vendor requests noisy host-level checks (kernel fuzzing), require additional insurance and a scoped time window.

Next steps (owner + due):
- Diego: Produce RBAC snapshot and run the analyzer (due 2025-11-12).
- Hannah: Export audit sample and produce SIEM mapping (due 2025-11-12).
- Marcus: Finalize sandbox and prepare AMI snapshot (due 2025-11-14).
- Rita: Approve sanitization plan (due 2025-11-12).

Revision history:
- 2025-11-04: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-11-07: added RBAC export commands and initial remediation items (Diego)
- 2026-02-10: updated priorities after internal review (Aisha)
